description: September 27 | 12:00 – 3:30 PM Lower Hall Gallery @ 12 | Brevik Hall @ 2 Join us at Aurora Town Square for National Day for Truth and Reconciliation! Reflecting upon the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, Mohawk-Ojibwe artist Sharon Rigby shares the stories of Indigenous individuals impacted by the residential school system and the Sixties scoop through a series of hand-crafted ribbon skirts. The exhibition begins in Lower Hall Gallery and extends to multiple sites across Aurora Town Square Opening Reception + Artist Talk and Tour – September 27, 12:00 – 2:00 PM Lower Hall Gallery (Level 1) Join us in Lower Hall Gallery (level 1) for refreshments, socialization, and an opportunity to meet the artist from 12-1pm. Remarks and tour commence at 1pm starting in, Lower Hall Gallery and ending in the Performance Hall Lobby (Level 2). All are welcome. Please be advised that this live event is unscripted. While every effort is made to foster respectful dialogue, the views expressed are those of the individuals and do not necessarily reflect those of the Aurora Cultural Centre. Some discussions may include mature themes or sensitive topics. Live Music with Red N Blue – September 27, 2:00 – 3:30 PM Brevik Hall (Level 2) Red N Blue is, Jeff Monague from the Beausoleil First Nation on Christian Island; Heather McIntyre who resides in Collingwood and has roots in Georgina Island First Nation; Michael Martyn is a settler who hails from Peterborough but now resides in Orillia. Their original music tells the story of the land and the First People to walk upon it.
